title: pala / palla
tip: Hold the double consonant a moment longer, as if pausing on it: pal-la. A single l flows straight on: pa-la.

title: caro / carro
tip: Single r is one quick tap of the tongue; double rr is a longer, stronger trill.

title: sera / serra
tip: Same as caro/carro: tap for r, roll for rr.

title: pena / penna
tip: Hold the n in penna slightly longer. The vowel before a double consonant is also a little shorter.

title: fato / fatto
tip: For tt, close your mouth on the t and hold briefly before releasing: fat-to.

title: nono / nonno
tip: Nonno has a held nn in the middle: non-no. Getting this wrong changes the meaning!

title: capello / cappello
tip: Two contrasts in one word: listen for the pp, then the ll, which both words share.

title: copia / coppia
tip: Hold the lips closed a moment longer for pp: cop-pia.

title: The gli sound
tip: Press the middle of your tongue flat against the roof of your mouth, close to 'lli' in 'million'. There is no hard g sound.

title: The gn sound
tip: Like 'ny' in 'canyon', said as one sound. There is no hard g sound.

title: c vs ch
tip: c + e/i sounds like English 'ch' (cena = CHEH-na). ch + e/i sounds like 'k' (chiesa = KYEH-za).

title: g vs gh
tip: g + e/i sounds like 'j' in 'jam'. gh + e/i is a hard 'g' as in 'get'.

title: sc vs sch
tip: sc + e/i sounds like 'sh' (pesce = PEH-sheh). sch + e/i, and sc before a/o/u, sound like 'sk'.

title: The Italian r
tip: Tap the tip of your tongue once against the ridge behind your top teeth, like the 'tt' in American 'butter'. Roll it for rr.

title: Stressed final vowels
tip: A written accent on the last vowel means the stress falls there: pe-RÒ, cit-TÀ. Say the final vowel clearly and firmly.
